immutable_state.instructions: Does the supplied production code avoid mutable domain state and model state transitions immutably?

criteria.pass: Domain types represent state with immutable properties (`val`) and immutable or defensively-copied collections, and state transitions return new values rather than mutating domain objects in place. Local variables inside parsing loops or a fold/loop accumulator holding an immutable value are acceptable.
criteria.fail: Any domain class stores mutable `var` properties, mutates collections or domain state in place, or shares mutable state across independent runs or calls.

domain_invariants.instructions: Do the domain types in the supplied production code own and enforce their intrinsic invariants at construction?

criteria.pass: Domain concepts with validity rules or domain behavior use dedicated types whose constructors/`init` blocks enforce their intrinsic invariants (pure enums or value types with no extra validity constraints also pass). Dedicated boundary, parser, formatter, or entry-point code passes when it delegates domain construction to validated domain types.
criteria.fail: Core logic passes around raw unvalidated primitives or untyped tuples (`Pair`, raw `Int`/`Char`/`String` tokens) for validated domain concepts, or enforces domain invariants only in parsers/callers while leaving domain constructors able to create invalid states.

boundary_separation.instructions: Does the supplied production code keep external I/O, input parsing, and output encoding or formatting strictly at the boundary, separate from core domain logic?

criteria.pass: External I/O, input parsing, and output formatting or encoding are isolated in dedicated boundary, parser, formatter, or entry-point code. Core domain types operate strictly on typed domain values and do not read files or streams, parse raw external text/tokens, or format protocol output.
criteria.fail: Core domain types directly perform external I/O, parse raw input tokens/characters/strings, or format protocol output strings, OR boundary parsing/formatting logic embeds core domain transition rules.
